next_paths.name: Forward deployed engineer
next_paths.what: An engineer embedded with customers who scopes, builds and ships LLM/agent solutions on the customer's data and systems.
next_paths.why_next: This course teaches the part an FDE does first: wire a model to a customer's tools with a loop you can explain and test, then prove it with evals and budgets.
learn: Scoping an agent use case with a customer (is it a workflow or an agent?)
Evals on customer data and acceptance criteria
Integrating with customer systems safely (least privilege, approvals)
Deployment, data-retention and security reviews
Explaining cost, latency and failure modes to non-engineers

evidence.what: Databricks 'AI Engineer - FDE (Forward Deployed Engineer)' posting (Greenhouse board, updated 2026-10-06)
Stripe 'Forward Deployed Engineer, Privy' posting (Greenhouse board)

next_paths.evidence_note: Across 10 public Greenhouse boards pulled on 2026-10-15, 143 of 4,414 open postings have 'Forward Deployed' in the title (most at Databricks). Titles were counted; job descriptions were not read in full. Vendor/infra companies skew the sample.

next_paths.name: Context engineering
next_paths.what: Deciding what goes into the model's window, in what order, and what is fetched just in time, compacted or left out.
next_paths.why_next: Lesson on context windows and the agent loop shows the window filling with tool results; this discipline is how production agents keep quality as the window fills.
learn: Context rot and attention budget
Just-in-time retrieval with lightweight identifiers
Compaction, tool-result clearing and structured note-taking
Sub-agents with clean contexts
Prompt caching layout (stable prefix first)

evidence.what: Anthropic engineering essay, 2025-09-29: context engineering as the successor to prompt engineering

Databricks 'Senior Staff Applied AI Engineer - Context Retrieval' and Elastic 'Principal AI Engineer - Context - Agents and Context' titles appear in public Greenhouse boards (2026-10-15); 4 of 20 sampled agent postings mention context window/engineering

next_paths.name: Agent evaluation and observability platforms
next_paths.what: Tools and practice for grading agent runs (outcome and trajectory), tracing every model and tool call, and gating releases on evals.
next_paths.why_next: The foundations course ends with a first golden-set eval and a run log; platforms turn those into dashboards, CI gates and production monitoring (track 6).
learn: Task, trial, grader, transcript, outcome vocabulary
pass@k vs pass^k
LLM-as-judge calibration against human labels
OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions and tracing back ends
Evals in CI for every prompt or model change

evidence.what: Anthropic engineering, 2026-01-09: eval vocabulary, grader types, pass@k vs pass^k, start with 20-50 real failures
Datadog 'Staff AI Engineer - Agent Observability' posting (2026-10-13)
Databricks 'Staff Software Engineer, Agent Quality' posting (2026-09-24)

next_paths.name: Harness engineering
next_paths.what: Designing the scaffolding around a model: system prompt, tools, context delivery, verification loops, memory, sandboxes, so an agent can finish real tasks.
next_paths.why_next: The 150-line loop you write here is a minimal harness; harness engineering is what that loop grows into for long-running work.
learn: Initializer + incremental coding-agent pattern
Progress files and clean committed state between sessions
Verification (tests, browser automation) inside the loop
Permissions and sandboxing
Which harness parts become unnecessary as models improve

evidence.what: Anthropic engineering, 2025-11-26: harness for long-running agents (initializer agent, progress log, JSON feature list)
Community list defining the discipline and collecting OpenAI/Anthropic sources (its annotations only; not an official definition)

next_paths.evidence_note: Mostly blogs and curated lists; the term is new. OpenAI's 'Harness Engineering' and 'Unrolling the Codex agent loop' pages returned HTTP 403 and were not read.

next_paths.name: Loop engineering
next_paths.what: Designing the systems that prompt coding agents repeatedly (goal loops, cron or event triggers, fresh context per item) instead of prompting by hand.
next_paths.why_next: You build the inner loop (model, tools, stop) here; loop engineering is the outer loop around it, with success criteria and budgets.
learn: Ralph-style one-item-per-iteration loops with success criteria
Triggers and schedules (CI failures, new tickets, nightly runs)
Stop conditions and token budgets for unattended runs
Fresh context per iteration to limit context rot
Cost control at API prices

evidence.what: The Pragmatic Engineer, 2026-07-14 (preview only, rest paywalled): definition, Ralph loops, built-in loop commands, skeptics
Anthropic 2025-11-26: agents working across many sessions with a progress log, the pattern loop engineering builds on

next_paths.evidence_note: Emerging: one paywalled newsletter post and vendor engineering notes; no job postings use the term. Do not oversell.

next_paths.name: Agent protocols (MCP)
next_paths.what: Standard ways to expose tools and data to any agent (Model Context Protocol) instead of one-off function schemas per app.
next_paths.why_next: You hand-wrote tool schemas and a registry; MCP is the shared version of that contract (track 4 of this roadmap).
learn: Host, client and server roles
Tools, resources, prompts
stdio vs Streamable HTTP
Authorization and tool-poisoning risks
Code Mode: models writing code against MCP tools

evidence.what: Analysis of 1,135 agentic AI listings (2026-03-31..05-22): MCP appears in 17-24% of postings that name an agent framework (publisher runs the job board)
Cloudflare, 2025-09-26: Code Mode, an argument for calling MCP through generated TypeScript
